newsitem.title: UK: Diana's dresses off to New York charity auction.
newsitem.headline: Diana's dresses off to New York charity auction.

text.p: A collection of dresses worn by Princess Diana during her ill-fated marriage were due to be flown to New York on Monday for an auction expected to raise millions of dollars for AIDS and cancer charities.
The 79 silk, satin, velvet and crepe evening gowns and fetching cocktail dresses from Britain's top designers wil be auctioned off at Christie's in New York on June 25.
Richard Branson, whose Virgin Group Atlantic airline is carrying the dresses, said in a statement he was happy to be able to help a worthy cause.
The collection features the best of British designers with gowns by Marc Bohan, Bruce Oldfield, Zandra Rhodes, the Emanuels, Victor Edelstein and Catherine Walker.
Christie's plans to hold a special lottery to select people who will attend the auction, which will be held in three sales rooms in New York. Up to 35 telephone lines will also be provided.
